title: ClickHouse and Hud Team Up to Add Runtime Intelligence to AI Software Development
partialText:
Artificial intelligence is transforming how software is built, but it is also creating new operational challenges for engineering teams. As AI coding assistants generate larger portions of production code, organizations are looking beyond code generation itself and focusing on how to verify, monitor, and safely deploy those changes.

ClickHouse and Hud are addressing that shift through a new partnership that combines observability with runtime intelligence. By integrating ClickHouse's ClickStack with Hud's Runtime Code Sensor, the companies aim to help developers evaluate AI-generated code before deployment, monitor its behavior after release, and accelerate troubleshooting when production issues occur.

A New Challenge for AI-Generated Code

The rise of AI-assisted programming has changed the pace of software development. According to the companies, AI currently generates or assists with 42% of the code developers ship, with that figure expected to climb to 65% by 2027.

While developers can produce software faster than ever, the question has become whether those changes can be trusted once they reach production. The partnership between ClickHouse and Hud is designed to provide engineering teams with production context throughout the software development lifecycle, helping them make more informed deployment decisions.

"AI is accelerating how quickly teams can generate code, but safely shipping it with high confidence requires production context," said May Walter, CTO & Co-Founder of Hud. "Hud and ClickHouse bring real production behavior at an unparalleled breadth and depth, so teams can build a production-aware AI SDLC: Gating before it ships, proactive verification once it is deployed, and fix issues as they arise - all using real runtime truth. Together with ClickHouse, we are bringing that intelligence across the entire AI SDLC."

Linking Infrastructure Signals to the Code Behind Them

The integration combines two complementary perspectives on software health.

ClickStack provides visibility across applications and infrastructure, allowing engineering teams to pinpoint the service, deployment, or endpoint where an issue has surfaced. Hud extends that view into the application's code, identifying the functions and code changes responsible for the observed behavior.

The platforms communicate through shared trace IDs, allowing engineers to move directly from an operational alert in ClickStack to detailed code-level analysis in Hud. Likewise, runtime intelligence gathered by Hud can provide additional context for issues initially identified through ClickStack.

For ClickHouse, the integration reflects a broader evolution in how observability data is being used.

"Our users already trust ClickHouse to store and query their Open Telemetry data at scale," said Mike Shi, Head of Observability at ClickHouse. "The shift now underway is from simply watching systems or investigating issues to using that data to make day-to-day engineering decisions. Hud connects observability data to the code and changes behind it, making the entire stack more useful for teams building and shipping software with AI."

Bringing Runtime Intelligence Into Deployment Decisions

Beyond troubleshooting, the partnership is intended to influence how engineering teams evaluate releases before they reach production.

According to the companies, runtime intelligence can help assess AI-generated pull requests using live production behavior rather than static analysis alone. Teams can identify higher-risk code changes that may require additional review while allowing lower-risk updates to move through deployment more efficiently.

The integration also supports release verification, regression detection, automated investigations, rollback workflows, and code-level remediation after deployment. When performance issues emerge—such as slower queries, increased resource consumption, or unexpected function behavior—Hud identifies the underlying code while ClickStack provides the broader operational picture needed to understand the impact.

A Production-Aware Development Lifecycle

The companies describe the collaboration as a step toward a production-aware AI software development lifecycle, where coding agents can make decisions based on recent operational data and application behavior instead of relying solely on source code.

That approach has already been adopted by monday.com, where engineering teams increasingly rely on AI during development.

"Like every modern engineering organization, a growing share of our code is now written with AI," said Rom Kadria, Senior Software Engineer at monday.com. "We write code much faster, but the challenge has shifted to shipping just as quickly while maintaining confidence that new code won't cause harm. ClickHouse gives us the wide operational picture at scale, while Hud gives us the runtime intelligence and next-level introspection needed to evaluate and ship AI-generated code confidently. When issues do arise, combining ClickHouse and Hud allows us to triage and resolve them quickly. For a company building with AI, that combination is the obvious choice."

Engineering teams can deploy the integration by installing the Hud SDK and connecting it with their ClickStack service, enabling runtime intelligence to work alongside the OpenTelemetry data they already collect. While the current release establishes the initial integration, ClickHouse and Hud say they plan to expand the partnership with deeper integrations over time.
